results.problem: High-recall nearest-neighbor search with inverted-file indexes
results.bound: \text{Exact top-}k \text{ of probed lists } S(\mathbf{q}) \text{ via certified screening}
results.previous_best: IVF-Flat (exact top-}k \text{ but scans all probed vectors)
results.quote: We prove that LYCHEE returns exactly the _k_ nearest vectors of the probed lists, which is the answer of an inverted-file search at full precision, while it reads a few hundred full vectors per query regardless of the number of probed lists.
Algorithm 1 runs in time _O_(|_S_(**q**)|(_m_+5)+_bD_+|_C_|log|_C_|+_V_(**q**)_D_) per query, where _V_(**q**) counts the survivors verified in Lines 6 to 10.
The extra space per query is _O_(_b_+|_C_|).

Device memory per vector is 2(_m_+5)+4_D_ bytes when full vectors reside on the GPU and 2(_m_+5)+4_D/s_ bytes when they reside in pinned host memory, since only the anchors stay on the GPU at full precision.
